publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents a variable gain instrumentation amplifier (IA) which does not use any passive resistor. It has utilized two-CCII+ cells and active load made of two-shunt connected nMOS transistors which produce a varying active load resistor when activated by adjustable DC voltage in the range of ±0.2 V. This tunable gain IA provides variable gain ranging in 40 dB to 80 dB. The input core of CCII+ cell has used symmetric bulk-driven current mirror OTA with self cascode load and partial positive feedback to ensure enhanced input common mode range (ICMR) and small signal performances even with low-DC voltage supply. The designed IA possess very high common mode rejection ratio (CMRR) and power supply rejection ratio (PSRR).

articleTitle: Correlation Between Heart Rate Variability Features
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Several features for heart rate variability (HRV) are being proposed in many studies. However, it is unclear whether new methods are contributing to knowledge or just duplicating the information represented by existing methods. Therefore, in this study, the correlation between different traditional and modern approaches to HRV analysis has been analyzed. The HRV features were extracted from signals of four classes of subjects acquired from PhysioNet databases. Three correlation coefficients, namely Pearson's correlation (PearCorr), Kendall's rank correlation (KendCorr), and distance correlation (DistCorr), have been used. PearCorr is sensitive to only linear relationships, whereas KendCorr and DistCorr are sensitive to both linear and nonlinear associations between variables. The experimental results suggest that traditional time-domain based features show a significant correlation with Poincaré plot-based features. The frequency-domain features show a considerable relationship with entropy-based complexity measures of HRV. The modern approaches to complexity analysis, such as heart rate asymmetry indices and phase entropy, do not show a significant correlation with other existing HRV features.

articleTitle: CPU Performance Modeling through Analysis of Primitive Operations
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Modern multi-core processors are complex because of their complicated memory hierarchies, superscalar issue of instructions, pipeline architecture, out-of-order execution and speculative execution due to branches in the program code. These features of the CPU are beneficial to improve the application performance. These processors have to be modelled to arrive at the trade-offs of design decisions such as power, time, throughput and latency. Modeling these complex micro-architectures is a very challenging task. In this work, we present a simple CPU modeling technique for data-parallel applications based on minimum offline profiling information and detailed static code analysis. This model, first identifies the primitive operations of the application kernels and then, based on the available offline profiled information, it estimates the performance of the given application kernel using either a SUM model or a MAX model. Experimental results show that an average estimation error of 7.19% and 41.4% is seen across data-parallel benchmarks from the Polybench suite for large and small problem sizes respectively on a multi-core CPU architecture.

articleTitle: Geometric approaches in time-frequency to grade tones in Chinese as a foreign language students
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Mandarin is a tonal language, meaning pitch is used to distinguish lexical meaning. Tone recognition occupies a significant role in learning Chinese. Automated grading metrics can provide language students with feedback in a non-threatening environment and without the high time and/or financial cost of individual feedback from a teacher. In this paper, we present some preliminary work on geometric measures in time-frequency to grade the quality of tone production in Chinese as a foreign language students. Our preliminary results show that the metrics can distinguish native from non-native speakers for all tones. The low computational cost of these metrics makes them especially suitable for mobile platforms.

articleTitle: Backstepping Control of Three-Phase Grid-Connected PV System
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this work, a backstepping control approach is applied on a three-phase grid-integrated PV system. In a conventional two-stage power conversion system, a boost and a DC-AC converters are used which are highly nonlinear systems. In conventional controller, these nonlinearities are ignored; they works only in linear region and hence operates in limited range. For efficient power transfer, tight regulation of DC-link voltage is required under generation and demand-side variations; so an effective controller is required. Backstepping control is a nonlinear control technique which takes care of useful nonlinearities in the system, helping to enhance system stability. The controller is designed by using dynamic equations of the system. A suitable Lyapunov function is chosen to verify the stability of the controller. The performances of the controller are evaluated under different dynamic conditions such as varying solar insolation, changing reactive and active power demand. The robustness of the presented controller is validated in simulation studies using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Modeling and Power Quality Analysis of Wind Energy Generation Arrangement with SMR MPPT
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Propose research work is examined a typical architecture of a Wind Turbine Generation Arrangement (WTGA) equipped with a generator operating at fixed speed. Presently SCIGs, DFIGs are being commonly utilized on WTGA, but synchronous generators (Alternator) are also broadly used. Different synchronous generators (SGs) configurations are suitable. Nevertheless, the multiple-pole Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSGs) is preferred ,Since it does not require rotor current for excitation due to permanent magnets in rotor assembly and also used without gearbox arrangement therefore it provides excellent performance owing to higher efficacy and less repairs, which also imply a decreasing of nacelle weight and declining of cost. What is more, the entire WTGA has been incorporated and simulated in MATLAB/Simulink interface (2017a). The WTGA has PMSG operated with fixed speed (12m/s) wind turbine. Maximum wind energy extraction is obtained using single switch mode rectifier (SSMR) scheme. Proposed system elements have been modeled with equations that clarify elements performance. In addition, the idea of optimal Power Point Tracking (MPPT) has been verified and presented in Simulink environment with the generator speed (rotor) according to instantaneous wind speed.

articleTitle: Hide Secret Information in Blocks: Minimum Distortion Embedding
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, a new steganographic method is presented that provides minimum distortion in the stego image. The proposed encoding algorithm focused on DCT rounding error and optimized that in a way to reduce distortion in the stego image, and the proposed algorithm produces less distortion than existing methods (e.g., F5 algorithm). The proposed method is based on DCT rounding error which helped to lower distortion and higher embedding capacity.

articleTitle: RF PIN Diodes Triggered Frequecny Reconfigurable Multiband (UMTS/Bluetooth/WiMAX) Antenna for Applications in Wireless system
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This research article presents applications for three wireless bands: Universal Mobile Telecommunication System (UMTS: 1920MHz-2170MHz), Bluetooth (2.402GHz-2.480GHz) and WiMAX (3.30GHz-3.80GHz) wireless system. Proposed antenna contains three quarter-wavelength stub printed on one surface for above said three applications and rectangular ground plane on opposite side. FR4 microwave substrate is used for design and analysis purpose and also the application bands are reconfigured by using three PIN diodes. Desired radiation patterns are obtained in expected principal planes of antenna. Also gain of the antenna remains almost constant in operating bands and maximum gain of 89%.

articleTitle: New Adiabatic Error Tolerant Adder I Architectures
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper proposes two architectures of 16-bit Adiabatic Error Tolerant Adder I (ETA I). The first architecture is based on adaptation of ETA I in Adiabatic domain and is termed as AETA-I. The approximate part in AETA-I uses large number of buffers and its delay dominates the computation time, thus not fully utilizing the benefits of Approximate Computing. The second architecture addresses this issue by modifying AETA-I (META-I), processing propagate and generate bits rather than actual input values. This modification reduces the number of buffers significantly (3.42 times) and culminates into reduction in pipeline depth, power and area. The proposed adders are implemented using Positive Feedback Adiabatic Logic (PEAL) and are validated using 45nm PTM HP technology parameters in Tanner T- Spice™. For a wider comparison, PEAL based 16-bit Kogge Stone Adder (KSA) is also implemented. The proposed MAETA-I architecture has a maximum power savings of 44.94% and 30.33% at 50MHz when compared with Adiabatic KSA and AETA-I respectively.

articleTitle: Deflection Analysis of Capacitive Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer with InP Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, the clamped circular CMUT model developed using thin plate Kirchhoff’s theory is utilized for structural analysis. The CMUT with wurtzite indium-phosphide nanowires as membrane material has been analyzed, and results discussed for resonant frequency, capacitance variation, pull-in/collapse voltage along with deflection profile. This has been found that CMUT with indium phosphide membrane is suitable for air-borne applications.

articleTitle: DSP Implementation of Hilbert Transform for Voltage Variation Tracking
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, the Hilbert Transform (HT) based detection scheme is presented for the identification of voltage variation events such as sag, swell, and interruption. The distinct feature of the proposed scheme is the utilization of a moving average filter along with the Hilbert transform and fuzzy system. Software implementation and hardware prototype were developed for real-time processing of voltage variations on floating-point DSP (TMS320F28379D) board. Experimental and simulation results are presented to validate the proposed scheme. Finally, the performance accuracy of the proposed algorithm validated and achieves promising results on the hardware.

articleTitle: Design of 100 W LDMOS based Power Amplifier for cellular applications
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents a design and implementation of a 100 W (50 dBm) power amplifier (PA) for the WCDMA base station application using laterally diffused metal oxide semiconductor (LDMOS) device which consists of two transistors integrated into a single package. To combine the output power of two transistors, active load combiner topology is adopted. This topology ensures that the optimum load impedance is maintained at the output of transistors, which provides high drain efficiency and high output power. A power amplifier is designed with this LDMOS transistor and its working is validated through measurement results. At 2.1 GHz, the measured gain of 10.8 dB, drain efficiency of 52.5% and output power more than 50 dBm is obtained. The effect of gate bias is also analyzed in measurement to show the relation of gain with gate bias variation.

articleTitle: Abnormal Moving Speed Detection Using Combination of Kernel Density Estimator and DBSCAN for Coastal Surveillance Radars
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of detection of abnormal moving speeds for a coastal surveillance radar. A new definition of normal moving speeds which is based on the historical radar data of maritime targets on the monitoring area is introduced. The historical radar data is mined by the cell-based method, unsupervised machine learning to obtain the vessel normal moving speeds in the monitoring area. Then a logic rule is applied to detect the abnormal targets. The proposed method is tested with real data from a coastal surveillance radar. The test results show that the false alarm rate (FAR) is equal zero. It is also shown that this kind of anomaly detection can be integrated into a coastal surveillance radar for the detection of the maritime illegal activities.

articleTitle: Design & Implementation of Low Power Delta Sigma ADC
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: The paper presents a multibit very low power consumption technique to design an ADC using op-Amp. An external biasing circuit is not required as op-amp with telescope used self-biasing method. The power & speed is optimized with integration of common gate & common source stages. It can be achieved by altering input & output biased current stages as per requirements. The reduction of complexity of circuit is done by offering less number of transistors in the circuit. The 0.25μm process technology used to design cascode telescope amplifier. The input and sampling frequency of cascode telescope amplifier is 1GHz & 106 M samples per second. Input voltage varied from 0 to 5V. The achieved power consumption of cascode telescope amplifier is 44.053 μw.

articleTitle: A Computational Model for the estimation of IR Attenuation in Duststorm with varying visibility
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: This paper presents an estimation of the propagation attenuation constant in duststorm at infrared wavelength. The log normal statistical parameters σ and μ of the dusty media aerosol size distribution are evaluated using the previously reported experimental data. Using detailed Mie scattering model and the curve fitted probability density function, the propagation attenuation constant, in the dusty medium at infrared wavelength, is computed. The computed attenuation is related to optical visibility where visibility is estimated using the same particle size distribution at wavelength equals to 0.55 micron. The results are compared with the measured data available in literature.

articleTitle: A Linear Time Side Match Vector Quantization Implementation
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Side match vector quantization (SMVQ) is slower than vector quantization (VQ). For each SMVQ index, it generates a state codebook SCB. The N codewords from the main codebook D are sorted by their side match distortions SMDs. The average execution times with N = 512 and 1024 are 18.528 and 46.052 seconds. In this paper, we propose an approach that can exploit any integer sorting algorithm. First, it assigns a modified side match distortion integer MSMD to each codeword. A codeword's MSMD is a function of its SMD. Next, it sorts the codewords in D by their MSMDs. This step can use any integer sorting algorithm. Our implementation uses the bucket sort algorithm. It reduces the SMVQ's time complexity from O(Nlog<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>N) to O(N + K), where K is the number of buckets. Experimental results verify that our implementation is faster. The average execution times with N = 512 and 1024 are 4.279 and 7.247 seconds. That is double the time of VQ. Also, the average execution times with N = 2048 and 4096 are 19.833 and 51.710 seconds.

articleTitle: Viscosity based liquid classification using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Every liquid has certain properties, which signifies its usage in various applications. One of the major property for identification of liquid is through the determination of its viscous behaviour. This paper aims at classification of different liquids by comparing their viscosity. A hardware has been designed to obtain the frequency of different liquids. A strategic relationship between the frequency of liquid and their viscosity has been significantly correlated by using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. A model has been designed using ANN which is a viable tool for classification of 49 different liquids on the basis of their frequencies. This helps in categorizing these liquids into 2 categories i.e. type 0 and type1. Promising results were obtained by the ANN model for different categories of liquids. High correlation coefficient 0.96521 and less Mean Square Error (MSE) 0.0145 were achieved which provides a framework for liquid identification based on their viscosity.

articleTitle: Hybrid SVM-LR Classifier for Powdery Mildew Disease Prediction in Tomato Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 7th International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
abstract: Tomato plant suffers from various severe diseases; powdery mildew being one of them. Weather conditions play a significant role in the development of powdery mildew disease in tomato plant which in turn reduces the growth of tomato fruit. Hence, an accurate and timely detection of powdery mildew is necessary to extenuate the economic losses caused by the disease. This paper aims to develop a hybrid of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression (LR) algorithm to predict powdery mildew disease in tomato plant. SVM is used to minimize the noise in data before the data is fed to LR classifier. Noise reduction is done using SVM classifier with the help of Adaptive Sampling based Noise Reduction (ANR) method. A real life Tomato Powdery Mildew Disease (TPMD) dataset has been used in this study to develop a prediction model using the proposed method. SVM and LR algorithms have also been used individually for developing the prediction models. Results indicate that the proposed classifier performs 3.06% better than SVM and 5.35% better than LR with an accuracy of 92.37%.
